report_meta.changelog: Added Recent Form section - actual Premier match results (5-4, 56% WR). Dust II and Inferno are perfect so far, Ancient/Anubis/Cache are 0% (1 game each).
report_meta.weekly_focus: Dust II is 3-0 in Premier and Ancient/Anubis/Cache are 0-1 each - worth weighting veto strategy toward Dust II/Inferno until the weaker maps get more reps.

high.label: High
high.meaning: Numbers are stable, trust the trend

med.label: Medium
med.meaning: Broad picture is solid, specific splits still settling

low.label: Low
low.meaning: Early days - treat as promising, not proven

players.name: the boy who lift
players.ct_detail: Aggressive peek on entry lanes to shut down T momentum early rather than sit passive.
players.t_detail: First through on every default execute, wins the opening duel more often than not.
players.good: Best entry success on both sides, ADR miles ahead of the squad - big sample so this is trustworthy
players.note: Team leans hard on him - if he's off, the whole T-side execute structure needs a backup plan
players.weapon_note: Noticeably stronger on M4A4 than M4A1-S (54% vs 44% HS) - worth actually running M4A4 on CT if he isn't already.

players.name: rosso
players.ct_detail: Sits mid/connector, reads info, calls the rotate.
players.t_detail: Trades directly behind the entry, calls the site once contact's made.
players.good: Balanced numbers everywhere, doesn't chase frags - exactly what you want calling the game
players.note: Nothing spikes as a standout stat, so the value here is leadership not raw firepower
players.weapon_note: Dead even on both rifles - consistency shows up in loadout choice too, not just role.

players.name: Sandz
players.ct_detail: Anchors a site alongside util (smoke/molly entrances) rather than isolated duels.
players.t_detail: Sets up the entry with smokes/flashes before the push.
players.good: CT entry success clearly beats his T-side numbers - genuinely reads a hold well, that instinct is real
players.note: Next step is sharpening the aim side (crosshair, spray control) so the good positioning converts into more kills - a trainable gap, not a talent gap
players.weapon_note: Most-used weapon overall is the P90 - tracks with a support role that plays a lot of eco and force-buy rounds rather than always full rifle economy.

players.name: Sy
players.ct_detail: Flexible position, held for the late-round 1v1/1v2.
players.t_detail: Second entry or lurk, depending on the call.
players.good: Best clutch numbers on the team (80% 1v1, 36% 1v3)
players.note: Nowhere near enough games yet - revisit once past 30-40 games
players.weapon_note: Near-identical HS% on both rifles - strong on whichever side he's on, though still a small sample like everything else with him.

players.name: Treb
players.ct_detail: Solo holds a site with util backing.
players.t_detail: Lurks rather than entries - plays off the clutch instinct.
players.good: Strongest CT numbers in the squad, solid 1v1 clutch rate (63%)
players.note: Clear gap between CT entry (56%) and T entry (40%) - biggest split on the team
players.weapon_note: Big gap between rifles (58% vs 37% HS) - AK is clearly the stronger weapon, worth noting given the T-side positioning gap is separate from this and about entries, not aim.

best_pairs.title: Highest win rate (small sample)
best_pairs.reasoning: 71% win rate over 7 games together - the best of any duo on the squad, though the sample is small. Every pairing involving Sy sits above the squad's baseline win rate, which is worth tracking as more games come in.

best_pairs.title: Most proven pairing
best_pairs.reasoning: 50 games together, 50% win rate - the biggest sample of any duo on the team and a reliable break-even return. Makes sense as a CT-side anchor pair given both read a hold rather than force duels.

best_pairs.title: Entry duo
best_pairs.reasoning: 28 games together, 50% win rate - confirms what the individual stats already suggested. Best fragger paired with the most reliable trader, and the data backs it up as the T-side engine.
